summary: Iteration 34 verification (Browse Businesses + Global Search featured/no-results + Public Track + Approvals Ready toggle + Place Order quick action). Backend pytest 12/12 passing (1 skipped due to seeded restaurants having no menu items; happy-path public-track validated via unit-level tests, 404 path verified). All frontend flows work: /businesses page renders 12 cards, category chips filter grid (All/Restaurants/Pharmacy/Grocery), Taxi/Courier chips navigate to /taxi-booking and /courier-order and show 'N online' hint (6 online), search filters cards by typed query (>=2 chars, 'roti' -> 1 card). Restaurant card click -> /restaurant/:id. Top nav shows 'Business' link (goes to /businesses); no 'Restaurants' or 'Car Rentals' links in nav. GlobalSearch on focus shows featured-partners-dropdown + search-cat-* chips + popular-search-* chips + featured-partner-* rows; nonsense query renders search-no-results with 5 no-results-suggestion-* and no-results-browse-all button. Public /t/invalid renders public-track-error 'Tracking link not found'. Customer /dashboard has quick-action-place-order -> /businesses. Admin Approvals: approvals-ready-toggle present and functional (default ON: 6 merchant apps filter to 1 with complete docs); record-docbadge-* rendered on rows.

minor.issue: Seeded restaurants (5) have zero menu items so end-to-end order creation for public-track happy-path test was not runnable. The endpoint itself works (404 for unknown verified). Recommend seeding at least one menu item per restaurant to enable e2e delivery tests.

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Seed at least 1 menu item per seeded restaurant so QA agents can exercise end-to-end order + public-track share flow.

(Regression note) The Order Tracking share button (data-testid share-tracking-btn) was NOT clickable in this run because creating a customer order requires menu items; verified button exists in OrderTrackingPage.js (line 240) via code review only.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py continues to grow (11k+ lines) - the new /search/featured, /drivers/online-count and /orders/{id}/public-track endpoints are fine but again all live in the mega-file. Extract into search_router.py / public_router.py.

GET /api/orders/{order_id}/public-track intentionally returns a curated subset (good), but returns raw driver_location (lat/lng) without checking if the driver is currently assigned+in-transit. If an order status is 'pending' or 'cancelled', the driver location still leaks. Consider gating driver_location behind status in {'assigned','picked_up','out_for_delivery'}.

BusinessSearch.js uses static category chips that call /taxi-booking and /courier-order. These are protected routes for taxi/courier customers - unauthenticated users clicking Taxi from /businesses will be sent to login. Consider a light-touch inline CTA that explains 'Sign in to book'.
